activation_observable: mean and p99 of the entrywise rescale factor applied to the momentum immediately before the polar iteration, printed once at end of run as precond_scale_mean and precond_scale_p99; plus the unchanged post-NS path's own scale for comparison. A value of exactly 1.0 means the edit did not engage.
competing_explanation: an effective learning-rate change. Renormalizing the momentum before orthogonalization alters the norm of the matrix fed to the polar iteration, and the iteration's output scale is set by that input; so a win could be nothing but a global step-size change that the same wave would reproduce by moving lr alone. This must be ruled out with an LR-matched arm or by showing the post-NS RMS is preserved.
falsifier: val_bpb of the reordered variant is within the measured within-wave band of its yoked control WHILE the activation observable shows the preconditioner is materially non-identity (pre-NS entrywise rescale ratio far from 1). That combination says the intervention engaged and did nothing. If instead the observable shows the rescale ratio sitting at ~1, the run is INCONCLUSIVE about the mechanism, not evidence against it.
mediator: the entrywise scale distribution of the momentum matrix AT THE MOMENT it enters Newton-Schulz. Orthogonalization is scale-equivariant in a way that discards entrywise second-moment information: normalizing the momentum by its running second moment BEFORE the polar iteration changes which singular directions the iteration is asked to equalize, whereas the same normalization applied AFTER only rescales an already-orthogonalized update and cannot change its direction.
name: precond_before_ortho

activation_observable: num_steps and step_ms_med, which move only if the iteration count is actually on the critical path at 512-wide matrices, plus the emitted ns_steps value itself so a config that silently failed to apply is distinguishable from one that applied and did nothing.
competing_explanation: host CPU contention setting step count independently of anything we changed. This is the dominant nuisance on this box -- byte-identical code has ranged 621 to 1021 steps -- so any step-count movement must be read against a control launched in the SAME wave, never across waves.
falsifier: reducing the iteration count changes NEITHER step count NOR val_bpb beyond the measured band, which would say the iteration is not on the critical path at this size and the axis is not worth further runs; or reducing it costs val_bpb by more than it buys in steps, which closes the direction downward.
mediator: the condition number of the orthogonalized update -- how close the polar iteration drives the singular values to 1 -- traded directly against the FLOPs and kernel launches spent on the iteration inside a wall-clock-bounded step.
name: ns_iteration_budget

activation_observable: mean Frobenius norm of the Muon-owned stacked matrices at the final step, printed as muon_weight_norm_final, together with the fraction of entries the cautious mask actually decayed, printed as wd_mask_frac -- the second number is what distinguishes a nominal coefficient change from a delivered one.
competing_explanation: weight decay never reaches equilibrium in this budget. A registered claim puts the equilibrium timescale at order 1000 steps for typical eta/lambda, so at ~1000 steps any effect may be an implicit warmup-shape change rather than the steady-state regularization the source papers measured, and the two are not distinguishable from the final loss alone.
falsifier: moving the decay coefficient across the range the literature disputes leaves val_bpb inside the band in a yoked pair, while the observable confirms the mean weight norm of the hidden matrices actually moved. Note one registered claim holds that Muon without weight decay converges FASTER initially, so this mechanism predicts a sign that may invert at our very short horizon; a null here is genuinely informative.
mediator: the weight norm of the Muon-owned 2D matrices over the run. The baseline applies a CAUTIOUS decay, masked to entries where update and parameter agree in sign, so the decay actually delivered to those matrices is strictly less than the nominal coefficient and its effective strength is data-dependent rather than set by the schedule.
name: decay_reaches_muon_matrices

activation_observable: embed_disp_ratio_first30 = ||wte.weight(step 30) - wte.weight(step 0)||_F / ||wte.weight(step 0)||_F, and head_disp_ratio_first30 for lm_head. Implemented as one clone of each tensor at step 0, one difference at step 30, then the clones are dropped; the two floats are printed AFTER the charged clock stops. Nothing touches muon_step_fused. Expected control value for the embedding is of order 0.2-0.5; ENGAGED means the treatment is below roughly half the control's. Print alongside warm_lrm_step10, the AdamW-group LR multiplier actually applied at step 10 -- exactly 1.000 means the ramp never engaged -- and lr_integral_rel, sum_t lrm_adam(t) divided by the control's, which should be ~0.985 so that the shape change is large while the integral change is small.
competing_explanation: An effective-learning-rate reduction in disguise. Every warmup lowers the LR integral, and this campaign already carries a registered opposing claim (o0_mgup_gain_confounded_by_effective_lr) about a step-size mask whose reported speedup was never separated from a 1.25x average-LR increase. The design is chosen so the two are far apart -- a 15-30 step ramp out of ~1015 removes only ~1.5% of the integral while cutting the first-step displacement by ~10x -- and the DISCRIMINATOR is a third arm that keeps the shape flat and instead scales EMBEDDING_LR / UNEMBEDDING_LR / SCALAR_LR down by exactly that measured integral fraction (lr_integral_rel). If the flat-but-scaled arm reproduces the warmup arm's val_bpb, the mediator is the integral and the mechanism is refuted. A second, cheaper explanation is loss-spike avoidance rather than curvature: if the control's first ~30 logged train_loss values show a spike or plateau that the treatment removes, the gain is stability, not the smoothness argument of b5_local_smoothness_scales_with_loss_gap; log the first 30 train_loss values in both arms to tell them apart.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-DEAD: in a slot-counterbalanced pair, embed_disp_ratio_first30 in the treatment is below half the yoked control's value (proving the first-30-step displacement really shrank) and val_bpb moves by less than the counterbalanced resolution 0.000174. That kills it: the enormous first embedding step is not costing anything at this operating point. DID-NOT-ENGAGE (inconclusive, not evidence against): embed_disp_ratio_first30 is unchanged, or warm_lrm_step10 prints 1.000. The two most likely causes are (a) the ramp was written on the wall-clock `progress` variable, where WARMUP_RATIO * 300s is already past by step 30 because a step is ~297ms, so the ramp never fires, and (b) the ramp was applied to all param_groups including Muon, where the polar iteration renormalises the update and the Muon arm silently becomes a pure LR-integral change. A separate NOT-A-TEST outcome: num_steps differs from the control by more than 0.3%, in which case the campaign's -0.063 bpb/e-fold step law rather than the mechanism explains the delta.
mediator: The size of the first ~30 parameter displacements of the Adam-owned token embedding and lm_head, measured as ||w_30 - w_0||_F / ||w_0||_F. WARMUP_RATIO is 0.0, and with exp_avg_sq zero-initialised an AdamW step at t=1 is a pure sign step of magnitude lr, so every embedding row touched by the first batch moves by EMBEDDING_LR * (512/768)^-0.5 = 0.735 in a single step against a unit-std normal init -- a displacement of order the parameter itself, taken before any curvature information exists and while the loss surface's local smoothness is at its largest. The mediator is that displacement ratio, NOT the learning-rate value: a short step-clocked ramp applied only to the four kind=='adamw' groups shrinks it by a factor of ~10 while removing only ~1.5% of the run's LR integral, and leaves the Muon groups (whose polar iteration discards update magnitude anyway, and for which the literature puts the optimal warmup fraction at 0.3% of tokens) untouched.
name: adam_group_warmup_only

activation_observable: lr_integral_ratio_adam_over_muon -- two Python float accumulators in the training loop, summing the LR multiplier actually written into the AdamW groups and into the Muon groups, divided at the end and printed after the charged clock stops. Exactly 1.000 = did not engage; a 0.3 floor over the second half predicts ~1.45. Report with adam_update_rms_ratio = (RMS of the AdamW-group parameter change over the last 50 steps) / (same over the first 50 steps), obtained by cloning only the small groups; this is the direct test of whether the Adam side self-anneals here as o0_adam_self_anneals_on_real_data claims, and it is the number that says whether the mechanism had any room to act.
competing_explanation: An effective-learning-rate increase on the single highest-LR group in the model. Flooring the AdamW multiplier raises the tail LR of the token embedding, which runs at 0.735 -- roughly 18x MATRIX_LR -- so any gain is equally consistent with 'EMBEDDING_LR is simply set too low', with no optimizer-family dissociation involved at all. DISCRIMINATOR: an integral-matched arm that leaves the shared cooldown shape untouched and instead raises EMBEDDING_LR / UNEMBEDDING_LR / SCALAR_LR by exactly the factor lr_integral_ratio_adam_over_muon reports. If that arm reproduces the effect, the mediator is the AdamW LR integral and this mechanism is refuted. A second competing explanation runs the other way: a non-zero terminal AdamW LR leaves the last iterate noisier, so a WORSE result may be last-iterate noise rather than the mechanism failing -- the existing `ema` variant axis (tail weight averaging, evaluated after the charged clock stops) separates 'the trajectory got worse' from 'the endpoint got noisier'.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-DEAD: lr_integral_ratio_adam_over_muon confirms the split reached ~1.4 and val_bpb is within 0.000174 of the yoked control -- the two optimizer families are not dissociated at this scale and one shared multiplier is fine. The mechanism is ALSO informatively killed if the floored arm is WORSE by more than the resolution, which would say the embedding and lm_head need the full anneal too and that o0_adam_self_anneals_on_real_data (measured on a 2-layer MLP on sklearn digits) does not transfer to a 124M LM. DID-NOT-ENGAGE (inconclusive): lr_integral_ratio_adam_over_muon prints 1.000, meaning the group filter matched nothing -- the loop currently sets group['lr'] for every group in one pass and the split must branch on group['kind'], so a variant keyed on anything else silently produces a byte-different control. Second not-engaged signature: adam_update_rms_last50 / adam_update_rms_first50 in the CONTROL is already below ~0.1, i.e. the Adam groups self-annealed on their own and the floor had nothing left to hold up.
mediator: The ratio of the LR integral delivered during the cooldown phase to the SPECTRALLY NORMALISED parameters versus to the SELF-ANNEALING ones: sum_t lrm_adam(t) / sum_t lrm_muon(t), which the baseline pins at identically 1.000. Muon's update is orthogonalised, so its step length does not shrink as the gradient shrinks and it sits on a last-iterate loss floor of order eta^2 that only driving eta to zero removes; the AdamW-owned embedding, lm_head, value-embeddings and per-layer scalars have a measured per-step update norm that falls with the gradient, i.e. they self-anneal and the same literature measures their optimal cooldown fraction at 0. baseline/train.py applies one get_lr_multiplier(progress) -- linear to exactly zero over the last 50% of the time budget -- to both families at once. The intervention floors the AdamW-group multiplier (e.g. at 0.3 of peak) while the Muon groups keep the full decay to zero, so the mediator moves from 1.00 to ~1.4-1.5.
name: cooldown_split_by_update_normalization

activation_observable: align_offset_steps = decay_onset_step - epoch_switch_step, where decay_onset_step is the first step at which lrm < 0.999 and epoch_switch_step is the first step at which the loader's integer `epoch` becomes 2. Both are single int counters in the training loop, printed after the charged clock stops. Baseline is expected within a few tens of steps of 0; ENGAGED means |align_offset_steps| > 100 and its sign matches the arm. Print with frac_epoch1_steps_at_peak (steps with epoch == 1 and lrm > 0.999, divided by all steps with epoch == 1; baseline ~1.0) and lr_integral_rel (sum_t lrm(t) relative to the control), and always read final_epoch off the SAME wave's control per L005 rather than assuming 2.0.
competing_explanation: A plain LR-integral change. Moving WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.50 to 0.35 raises sum_t lrm by ~7.5% and moving it to 0.65 lowers it by ~7.5%, and b3_base_lr_dominates_schedule_shape says the LR scale should dominate schedule shape -- so a MONOTONE response across the two arms is a base-LR effect wearing a data-alignment label. This is exactly why only an asymmetric (non-monotone) response counts, and why the discriminating third arm holds the integral fixed: shift the onset earlier AND raise the peak so lr_integral_rel is within 0.5% of 1.000. If the integral-matched arm shows nothing while the raw arms show a monotone trend, the mechanism is refuted and the campaign has instead measured a base-LR gradient. A second cheap explanation is step count -- WARMDOWN_RATIO costs no FLOPs, so num_steps must match the control within 0.3% or the -0.063 bpb/e-fold step law explains the delta instead.
falsifier: Run WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.35 and at 0.65 as two slot-counterbalanced pairs; align_offset_steps must move to roughly +150 and -150. ENGAGED-AND-DEAD: align_offset_steps confirms both shifts and BOTH arms land within 0.000174 of their controls -- the alignment carries no weight and b3_cooldown_fraction_plateau (any cooldown fraction in 0.4-0.95 is equivalent for normalized optimizers) wins. CONFIRMED only by an ASYMMETRY: the two arms must move val_bpb in OPPOSITE directions by more than the resolution. A symmetric degradation on both sides means only that 0.5 sat at an interior optimum of a smooth curve and says nothing about data repetition; a monotone response across the two arms is the LR-integral confound below, not this mechanism. DID-NOT-ENGAGE (inconclusive): align_offset_steps did not move -- most likely because host load changed throughput and the wall-clock schedule re-aligned itself -- or the yoked control reports final_epoch 1.0, in which case there is no second pass for the mechanism to act on and every arm in the wave is inconclusive by construction.
mediator: The alignment offset, in optimizer steps, between the LR decay onset and the moment the training data starts repeating: align_offset_steps = decay_onset_step - epoch_switch_step. The schedule is clocked on wall time (progress = total_training_time / TIME_BUDGET) with WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5, and the run ends at final_epoch 2.0 over a fixed dataset, so at the current throughput the decay onset lands almost exactly on the epoch-1 -> epoch-2 boundary: the ENTIRE first-exposure pass runs at peak LR and the ENTIRE repeated pass runs under decay. That coincidence is not a schedule anyone chose -- it is an accident of the frozen packing loop's throughput, and L005 shows the same benchmark ran at final_epoch 1.0 when host load was different. The mediator is therefore how much peak-LR budget is spent on tokens the model has never seen versus tokens it is memorising for the second time, and it is a data-side quantity that no pure-schedule paper in the registry controls for.
name: lr_peak_spent_on_first_exposure

activation_observable: muon_lr_factor_by_shape -- the list of (shape, applied LR multiplier) pairs read off optimizer.param_groups after the charged clock stops. Control must show 1.0 for (512,2048) and treatment 0.5; a treatment printing 1.0 means the edit did not engage. Pair it with cproj_norm_final and cfc_norm_final, the Frobenius norms of the (512,2048) and (2048,512) stacked Muon groups at the last step, also computed after the clock stops (two reductions, free). Optional in-loop version: cproj_angular_step_med, the median over steps of ||group_lr * update||_F / ||param||_F for the (512,2048) group -- but only if it is accumulated on-device and reduced at the end, never with a per-step .item().
competing_explanation: A partial global learning-rate reduction. The intervention only ever LOWERS an LR, on about a third of the Muon parameters, so a gain is equally consistent with 'MATRIX_LR = 0.04 is simply too high' -- a base-LR change, which b3_base_lr_dominates_schedule_shape says should dominate any structural story, and which is the effective-LR confound that has already bitten this campaign. DISCRIMINATOR ARM: keep the clamp and instead scale MATRIX_LR for ALL Muon groups by 0.83, the parameter-weighted mean of the applied-LR change (two thirds unchanged, one third halved). If the flat arm reproduces the shape-aware arm's val_bpb, this is effective LR, not shape awareness. A cheaper and sharper second discriminator runs the other way: RAISE only the (512,2048) group by 2x, to 4x the rule. If both directions hurt by more than the resolution, that group sits at an interior LR optimum the data chose and the sqrt(d_out/d_in) prescription is not what is being measured.
falsifier: Replace max(1.0, shape[-2]/shape[-1])**0.5 with (shape[-2]/shape[-1])**0.5 in MuonAdamW._step_muon -- a one-line edit in the Python wrapper, OUTSIDE the fullgraph-compiled muon_step_fused, costing zero FLOPs and zero kernels. ENGAGED-AND-DEAD: muon_lr_factor_by_shape shows the (512,2048) group at 0.5 in the treatment and 1.0 in the control, cproj_norm_final has fallen relative to the control, and val_bpb is inside 0.000174 -- the clamp is not load-bearing at 512 width and the sqrt(d_out/d_in) rule has no special status here. DID-NOT-ENGAGE (inconclusive): muon_lr_factor_by_shape still prints 1.0 for (512,2048), meaning the edit landed but the group enumeration did not match -- the Muon groups are built from sorted({p.shape for p in matrix_params}), so a variant that keys on parameter NAMES rather than shapes silently produces a byte-different control. Second not-engaged signature: cproj_norm_final is unchanged despite the halved factor, which would mean the down-projection's norm is set by the data rather than by its LR and the mediator never moved.
mediator: The per-matrix angular step -- applied update Frobenius norm divided by parameter Frobenius norm -- for the fan-in-heavy 2D matrices. MuonAdamW._step_muon sets the group LR to lr * max(1.0, d_out/d_in)**0.5, which equals the spectral rule sqrt(d_out/d_in) ONLY where d_out >= d_in. At n_embd = 512 the clamp is inactive for the square attention matrices (512x512, factor 1.0 = rule) and for the MLP up-projection (2048x512, factor 2.0 = rule), but it is ACTIVE for the MLP down-projection (512x2048): the rule prescribes 0.5 and the code applies 1.0, exactly 2x the shape-consistent rate; ve_gate (4x32) gets 2.83x. mlp.c_proj is about one third of all Muon-owned parameters, it is the MLP's write path into the residual stream, and it is ZERO-initialised, so the rate at which its norm grows over the first ~50 steps sets the residual gain of every block from step 0. The mediator is that group's angular step, which the clamp inflates by exactly 2x relative to the rule the literature says transfers.
name: muon_shape_clamp_on_fan_in_heavy_matrices

activation_observable: namo_scale_mean, namo_scale_p10 and namo_scale_p90 -- the per-step scalar applied to the orthogonalised update, accumulated into a preallocated on-device buffer indexed by step and reduced AFTER the charged clock stops. It is computed in the Python MuonAdamW._step_muon from stacked_grads.norm() taken BEFORE the in-place lerp_ inside muon_step_fused mutates that tensor, and passed in as a 0-D DEVICE tensor folded into lr_t, so nothing is added inside muon_step_fused (which is @torch.compile(fullgraph=True)) and no host sync is added to the step. ENGAGED means namo_scale_mean in 0.95-1.05 AND namo_scale_p90/namo_scale_p10 > 1.3. A mean far from 1.0 does not mean 'engaged more' -- it means the arm is a disguised LR change and must be rebuilt.
competing_explanation: An effective-learning-rate change, and this is the failure mode the registry already documents twice: o0_mgup_gain_confounded_by_effective_lr describes a step-size mask whose recommended parameter is literally the argmax of its own 1.25x average-LR inflation, and o2_namo_needs_roughly_ten_times_the_muon_learning_rate records that NAMO's authors had to sweep a disjoint, ~9x higher LR grid, so their reported win is not separated from turning the LR up. The DISCRIMINATOR is namo_scale_mean itself: an arm whose mean scale is 1.00 +/- 0.05 has, by construction, the same LR integral as its yoked control, and the only surviving difference is the step-to-step VARIATION of the step length -- if the effect survives at namo_scale_mean = 1.0, it is not an LR change. A second competing explanation is throughput: two extra norm reductions per Muon group per step. Because this scope is input-pipeline bound (~94% of charged time is the frozen Python packing loop), the prediction is num_steps within 0.3% of the control; if num_steps moves more than that, the -0.063 bpb/e-fold step law, not the mechanism, explains the result.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-DEAD: namo_scale_mean sits in 0.95-1.05 (so the arm is scale-preserving and the LR integral matches the control) while namo_scale_p90 / namo_scale_p10 exceeds ~1.3 (so the step length genuinely varied over training), and val_bpb is within 0.000174 -- at ~1015 steps, re-coupling step length to gradient magnitude buys nothing. DID-NOT-ENGAGE (inconclusive): namo_scale_mean == 1.000 with p90/p10 below 1.05, i.e. the ratio saturated -- the usual causes are the second-moment buffer being warm-started from the first gradient so the ratio is pinned at 1, or the bias corrections cancelling. A DIVERGENCE (the fast-fail at train_loss > 100) is ALSO a not-engaged outcome under this design and not evidence against the mechanism: the registered boundary claim o2_namo_needs_roughly_ten_times_the_muon_learning_rate says the scalar changes the update scale by ~9x, so the arm MUST be built scale-preserving -- divide the scalar by its own running mean, or fold a compensating constant into MATRIX_LR -- and namo_scale_mean is the number that proves it was.
mediator: The information content of the Muon step LENGTH. After the polar iteration the update is spectrally normalised, so its magnitude is set entirely by the LR schedule and carries NO gradient-magnitude information: the step does not shrink as the model approaches a stationary point, does not grow when the loss surface presents a large coherent gradient, and does not react to the momentum buffer decohering. The intervention multiplies the orthogonalised update by one scalar per matrix group -- the bias-corrected ratio of the momentum Frobenius norm to the running RMS of the gradient Frobenius norm -- which re-couples step length to how large and how coherent the current gradient is while leaving the direction exactly orthogonal. The mediator is the per-step ratio ||applied update||_F / ||orthogonalised update||_F, a constant equal to the LR in the baseline and a measured time series under the treatment. The source measured this at 124M nanoGPT with 491,520 tokens per step -- essentially this benchmark's 524,288 -- for -0.0084 nats, roughly 0.003 bpb, about 17x the counterbalanced resolution.
name: namo_restores_gradient_magnitude_to_muon_step

activation_observable: embed_moment_fill and head_moment_fill = mean|exp_avg| / sqrt(mean(exp_avg_sq) + 1e-20) over the token-embedding and lm_head parameters, read out of optimizer.state AFTER the charged clock stops (two reductions each, zero cost in the training loop, nothing near muon_step_fused). Baseline expectation is ~0.33 in the noise-dominated limit at b1 = 0.8 and ~0.16 at b1 = 0.95. ENGAGED means the treatment value differs from its yoked control's by more than 30%. Print with adam_beta1_by_group, the list of beta1 values actually held by each AdamW group at the end of the run -- it is what distinguishes 'two groups changed' from 'the module constant changed all four'.
competing_explanation: An effective-learning-rate change in disguise. Lengthening the first-moment window changes the delivered update MAGNITUDE, not only its noise content: |exp_avg| / sqrt(exp_avg_sq) falls for noise-dominated coordinates and rises for signal-dominated ones, so the step size on the embedding moves without any LR constant appearing to change -- exactly the confound this campaign has already been bitten by. The DISCRIMINATOR is the observable itself: multiply the changed groups' LR by the measured ratio (control fill / treatment fill) and re-run; if that magnitude-matched arm reproduces the effect, the mechanism was step size, not averaging. A second competing explanation is attribution: the embedding runs at LR 0.735 while the lm_head runs at 0.0049, a 150x gap, so an effect could come entirely from the embedding while the cited claims specifically name the lm_head as the largest-variance layer. The split arms -- beta1 raised on the embedding only, then on the lm_head only -- are what attribute it, and if the whole effect is embedding-side then the gradient-variance mechanism is not the one operating.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-DEAD: embed_moment_fill and head_moment_fill move by more than 30% from the yoked control's values and adam_beta1_by_group shows exactly two of the five groups changed, while val_bpb stays inside 0.000174. DID-NOT-ENGAGE (inconclusive): the fill factors are unchanged. The likely cause is that the variant edited the ADAM_BETAS module constant, which changes ALL FOUR AdamW groups at once and is a different, cruder experiment; the per-group version must write group['betas'] for the wte and lm_head groups in setup_optimizer, since the AdamW path re-reads group['betas'] every step. NOTE that two registered claims predict OPPOSITE signs here: the gradient-variance claims say more averaging on the two highest-variance layers helps, while o1_short_horizon_implies_lower_momentum derives optimal alpha = 1-beta proportional to b * T^(-1/2), i.e. a ~1015-step horizon wants beta FURTHER from 1, not closer. A significant result in either direction is therefore informative and only a null is a null -- which also means the arm should be run at beta1 = 0.95 and at beta1 = 0.6 as a pair, not in one direction only.
mediator: The number of independent minibatch gradients averaged into one update to the two layers that carry the largest stochastic gradient variance. ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.95) is shared by all four AdamW groups, so the token embedding and lm_head -- measured in the literature as the highest- and second-highest-variance layers of a 130M LM -- are updated from a first moment with an effective window of 1/(1-0.8) = 5 steps, while the Muon-owned matrices run at momentum 0.95 (window 20) and are additionally orthogonalised, which discards noise magnitude entirely. The mediator is the per-group first-moment fill factor mean|exp_avg| / sqrt(mean exp_avg_sq): for noise-dominated coordinates it is about sqrt((1-b1)/(1+b1)) = 0.33 at b1 = 0.8 and 0.16 at b1 = 0.95, and it rises toward 1 for signal-dominated ones, so it measures directly what fraction of each delivered update is signal rather than minibatch noise. The intervention raises beta1 for the wte and lm_head groups only.
name: momentum_window_on_the_high_variance_groups

activation_observable: branch_out_rms_mean -- the mean over all 16 sub-module outputs (8 attn, 8 mlp) of the RMS of the tensor that is added to the residual stream, measured on one fixed batch in a single eager forward AFTER the charged clock stops (use model._orig_mod with forward hooks; never inside the compiled training forward, which would graph-break). Treatment MUST read 1.000000 +/- 0.001 by construction of rms_norm; any other value means the edit did not land. Emitted by EVERY arm including the control, so 'engaged' is separable from 'took some value' -- the control reads its own trained value and that number is the mediator's baseline. Second number, same block: resid_rms_growth = RMS(x entering the final block) / RMS(x0 after the embedding norm), which is the quantity the mechanism claims to compress.
competing_explanation: (1) THROUGHPUT, the standing confound on this box. 16 extra normalization kernels per forward and their backward change step_ms_med, and the campaign's own step law converts step count straight into bpb at -0.063 to -0.0687 per e-fold; a 1% step-count loss is ~0.0007 bpb, four times the counterbalanced resolution. Discriminating observation: num_steps and step_ms_med read off the SAME wave's yoked control, plus gpu_span_ms_med from the loader_slack_prices_gpu_flops mechanism -- if gpu_slack_frac stays positive the added kernels are free and no step-law correction applies. (2) AN EFFECTIVE LEARNING-RATE CHANGE ON c_proj. Normalizing a sub-module's output makes the loss exactly invariant to the scale of that sub-module's output projection, which changes the effective step size Muon delivers to those matrices; a win could then be reproduced by rescaling matrix_lr on the c_proj groups alone, with no residual-geometry content. Discriminating observation: the mean Frobenius norm of the c_proj matrices at the end of the run -- if it diverges from the control's while resid_rms_growth is unchanged, the effect is a step-size effect wearing a geometry costume.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-INERT (kills the mechanism): branch_out_rms_mean reads 1.000 +/- 0.001 and resid_rms_growth differs from the yoked control's by more than 2x, yet val_bpb is inside the counterbalanced resolution 0.000174 of that control at equal step count -- residual-stream amplitude growth is then simply not a binding constraint at depth 8 / ~1015 steps, and the 0.09-0.11 nat Peri-LN gains reported at 400M-3.2B / 30B tokens are a depth-compounding effect that does not reach here. DID-NOT-ENGAGE (says nothing about the mechanism): branch_out_rms_mean is not 1.000, which means the norm was inserted after the residual add, or on the block input only, or the hook is reading the pre-norm tensor -- re-run, do not score. One registered claim already predicts the inert outcome for the wrong-sign reason: b5_keel_gain_is_backloaded_and_data_hungry reports this family of architectures being WORSE early and only overtaking Pre-LN late, and this benchmark is 100% 'early' (final_epoch 2.0, ~0.5B tokens), so an inert-or-harmful result must not be read as 'normalization placement does not matter', only as 'it does not pay inside 300 charged seconds'.
mediator: The branch-to-stream amplitude ratio: RMS(sub-module output) / RMS(residual stream at that depth), and therefore the depth-growth rate of the residual-stream norm. In the baseline (baseline/train.py:125-128, x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x))) this ratio is unconstrained -- it is set by whatever norms c_proj happens to train to, on top of a stream that is itself rescaled every block by resid_lambdas[i] and re-injected with x0_lambdas[i]*x0. Wrapping each sub-module OUTPUT in the existing rms norm() pins the numerator to exactly 1 for every block, so each block's contribution to the stream is amplitude-decoupled from its trained weight scale and the stream can grow at most like sqrt(depth) instead of multiplicatively. The intervention adds 2 RMSNorms per block (16 total at depth 8) and changes no parameter count.
name: periln_branch_output_norm
notes: NOT implemented in tools/make_variant.py -- new generator code. activation_observable: lmhead_expavg_to_grad_rms -- RMS(optimizer.state[lm_head.weight]['exp_avg']) / RMS(lm_head.weight.grad), sampled every 32 steps by appending two 0-dim CUDA tensors to a Python list and converted with .item() only AFTER the charged clock stops (the _mtp_hist pattern already in make_variant.py), so no synchronization is added to the step. Reported as the median over samples, emitted by EVERY arm including the control. Computed in the Python wrapper, OUTSIDE adamw_step_fused, which is @torch.compile(dynamic=False, fullgraph=True): a norm or a print inside that function would graph-break or force a recompile, and b1_optimizer_fusion_break_costs_loss records a pure-numerics loss regression from exactly that class of accident. Interpretation: the value sits at sqrt((1-b1)/(1+b1)) if the lm_head gradient is pure noise and ABOVE it by the amount the gradient is temporally correlated, so this one number reports both that the edit engaged and how much signal there was to average.
competing_explanation: AN EFFECTIVE STEP-SIZE CHANGE ON THE UNEMBEDDING. adamw_step_fused applies bias correction (bias1 = 1 - beta1**step), so the asymptotic update scale is preserved, but the early-step scale and the response to the linear-decay LR schedule are not; a win could therefore be nothing more than 'unembedding_lr=0.004 was mistuned', which an lr-only arm at 0.7x and 1.4x would reproduce at zero implementation cost. Discriminating observation: the ratio RMS(update)/RMS(lm_head.weight) at end of run -- if the momentum arm wins while that ratio is statistically unchanged from the control, the win is not a step-size effect. Secondary cheaper explanation: any change to the lm_head group also changes how the softcap (15*tanh(z/15)) saturates, so check that the fraction of |logits| above the softcap knee did not move.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-INERT (kills the mechanism at this operating point): lmhead_expavg_to_grad_rms moves from the control's band to the band predicted for the new beta1 -- for pure noise the ratio is sqrt((1-b1)/(1+b1)), i.e. 0.333 at beta1=0.8 and 0.160 at 0.95 -- yet val_bpb sits inside 0.000174 of the yoked control. That would say unembedding gradient noise is not what limits this run, which is a priori plausible and is the reason to measure it: the cited studies used 131k tokens/step and this benchmark uses 524288, so the lm_head gradient here is already averaged over 4x more tokens and its variance is ~4x lower before any momentum change. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: lmhead_expavg_to_grad_rms is unchanged from the control -- the beta1 edit landed on the wrong group (the baseline builds five AdamW groups and lm_head is the first, index 0; an edit to the shared adam_betas tuple would move ALL of them and is a different, confounded experiment).
mediator: The effective temporal averaging window applied to the noisiest tensor in the model: 1/(1-beta1) steps of the AdamW first moment on the lm_head parameter group ONLY. The baseline runs adam_betas=(0.8, 0.95) for every AdamW group (baseline/train.py setup_optimizer), so the unembedding -- the layer with the largest measured stochastic gradient variance -- is averaged over ~5 steps, the SHORTEST horizon in the model, while Muon gives the hidden matrices an effective 20-step Nesterov horizon at momentum 0.95. The intervention raises beta1 on the lm_head group alone, changing the fraction of the unembedding update that is minibatch noise rather than persistent signal. No other group, no other hyperparameter, one number in one param_group dict.

notes: NOT implemented in tools/make_variant.py -- new generator code, and it needs a new per-group beta override rather than a change to the shared adam_betas argument. activation_observable: qk_prenorm_rms_mean -- the mean over layers and sampled steps of RMS(q) and RMS(k) measured BEFORE the norm() call site, emitted by EVERY arm including the control. This is a REQUIRED CHANGE to the observable already in tools/make_variant.py under cfg['noqknorm'], which today replaces the norm with a probe and therefore prints q_rms_mean / k_rms_mean in the treatment ONLY: with nothing to compare against, 'engaged' cannot be distinguished from 'took some value', which is precisely the unfalsifiability the precond mechanism's own comment warns about. With the probe unconditional, the control must read 1.000 downstream of its norm and its own pre-norm value upstream, and the treatment's departure from 1.0 is the engagement number. Secondary: attn_logit_rms on one fixed batch after the clock stops.
competing_explanation: THE PROBE, NOT THE MISSING NORMALIZATION. The existing implementation appends to a Python list inside GPT.forward, which is inside torch.compile(model, dynamic=False); a list append graph-breaks the compiled region, and the resulting step-time change flows through the step law into val_bpb with no attention content whatsoever. This is the cheaper explanation for ANY effect this arm shows and it must be ruled out first. Discriminating observation: run a PROBE-ONLY arm that inserts the same probe while KEEPING q, k = norm(q), norm(k) -- it is the correct control for this mechanism, it is also what makes the observable comparable across arms, and if it alone moves step_ms_med the mechanism cannot be scored from the current implementation at all. Second competing explanation: throughput in the other direction -- removing 2 norms per layer is a FLOP saving, and under loader_slack_prices_gpu_flops that saving is predicted to buy nothing, exactly as L011 measured for the Newton-Schulz iteration count.
falsifier: The registered evidence predicts HARM, so this mechanism is falsified by an improvement as much as by a null. ENGAGED-AND-INERT: qk_prenorm_rms_mean departs from 1.0 by more than 2x (the trained q/k scale really did leave the pinned value) yet val_bpb is inside 0.000174 of the yoked control -- attention temperature is then not a binding degree of freedom at depth 8 with a 2048 context and an SSSL window pattern, and the whole q/k-scale sub-family can be closed on one wave. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: qk_prenorm_rms_mean stays at 1.000 -- either the norm was not removed, or the probe is reading the post-norm tensor; the run says nothing. A LOSS larger than the band with the observable confirming departure is the predicted CONFIRMING outcome and should be recorded as such, not as a failure: it converts two imported claims about removing normalization statistics into a measurement on this system, and it validates q_rms as an instrument for later interventions that MODIFY the temperature (a learned scalar, a depth-dependent scale) instead of removing it.
mediator: The RMS of q and k entering FlashAttention, and hence the scale of the pre-softmax logits -- the attention temperature. baseline/train.py:97 applies q, k = norm(q), norm(k) AFTER rotary, which pins both to RMS exactly 1 regardless of what c_q and c_k train to, fixing the logit scale at head_dim-determined values for the whole run and at every depth. Removing that norm hands the temperature back to the optimizer: the logit scale becomes a trained quantity that can drift with the weight norms over the run and differ across depth. The mediator is the pre-softmax logit RMS, not the presence of a norm() call.

activation_observable: mtp_aux_loss_drop (mean aux CE over the first 100 steps minus the mean over the last 100) together with mtp_grad_norm_frac (MTP_W * aux / (aux + train_loss)), both already emitted by tools/make_variant.py under cfg['mtp'] and accumulated as GPU tensors converted only after the charged clock stops. Engaged means mtp_aux_loss_drop > 0.1 AND mtp_grad_norm_frac > 0.02; a drop near zero with a nonzero share means the term is present but not learning, which is a non-activation and not evidence against supervision density. peak_vram_mb and num_steps must be read alongside them, because for this mechanism they are part of the activation test.
competing_explanation: MEMORY AND THROUGHPUT, and here they dominate the science. At this operating point one micro-batch is DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 x 2048 = 262144 positions and the vocabulary is 32768, so a single logits tensor is 17.2 GB in bf16 and 34.4 GB after the baseline's logits.float(); the auxiliary head materializes a SECOND one plus its own softcap temporary. The cheapest explanation of any result from this arm is therefore an allocator regime change -- OOM, expandable-segment thrash, or a step-count drop -- and not supervision density at all. Discriminating observations, in order: peak_vram_mb versus the control's, num_steps and step_ms_med from the same wave, and gpu_span_ms_med / gpu_slack_frac from loader_slack_prices_gpu_flops, which is what decides whether the extra vocab GEMM is free or not. If step count falls, score nothing until the arm is re-run at a micro-batch that restores it, because the step law converts a step-count loss directly into bpb.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-INERT ON THE METRIC THAT COUNTS: mtp_aux_loss_drop > 0.1 nats and mtp_grad_norm_frac > 0.02 (the auxiliary head is learning and is a real share of the objective) while val_bpb is inside 0.000174 of the yoked control at equal step count. o2_namo_train_loss_gain_is_ten_times_its_val_loss_gain is the reason to expect exactly this and is why train_loss MUST NOT be scored: at 124M and 50K steps a 0.10-nat train-loss gain bought only 0.008-0.019 val, so an objective-side intervention that improves fit can be worth ten times less on val than it looks. If the smoothed train loss improves and val_bpb does not, the mechanism is falsified for THE GOAL even though it engaged. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: mtp_aux_loss_drop ~ 0 -- the auxiliary path is dead, which is a live risk because mtp_proj is zero-initialized and shares lm_head, so at step 0 the aux logits equal the main logits and the only gradient into mtp_proj comes through that shared head. THIRD FAILURE MODE, check first: the run OOMs or step count collapses (see competing_explanation).
mediator: The number of independent supervised targets per token position per forward pass: 1 (next token) -> 2 (next token and t+2 through an auxiliary zero-initialized projection into the SHARED lm_head). The physical quantity is supervised gradient signal extracted per token of a FIXED dataset. This matters at this operating point specifically because final_epoch is 2.0: the 300-second budget already makes two passes over the same data, so more supervision per token is one of the few ways left to add signal without adding data, and it costs one extra vocab-width GEMM rather than the second backward pass that the variance-reduction route requires.
