notes: IMPLEMENTED and never run: cfg['mtp'] exists in tools/make_variant.py with its observables, and tools/direction.py lists it as an objective mechanism. No registered claim measures multi-token prediction itself -- the objective family holds 3 claims, 1 usable, against 20 fetched papers of which 17 are unread. The claims above constrain how a result must be INTERPRETED (train-vs-val decoupling at 124M; the price of buying extra gradient signal with a second backward) and do not supply a prior on the sign. That gap is a reason to extract from the 17 unread papers before spending the slot, and it is stated here rather than papered over with a claim that does not exist.

activation_observable: gpu_slack_frac = 1 - gpu_span_ms_med / step_ms_med, printed by EVERY arm including the control, alongside gpu_span_ms_med. gpu_span_ms is measured with a pair of torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) recorded at the top of the micro-step loop and after optimizer.step(); recording an event does not synchronize, and elapsed_time is queried for all steps only AFTER the charged clock stops, so the instrument cannot move val_bpb or the step count (2 events x ~1015 steps is negligible). Values: gpu_slack_frac > 0.1 means the free-FLOPs regime holds for this run; ~0 means the GPU is the critical path and every FLOP added from here is paid for at the step law's exchange rate of -0.063 to -0.0687 bpb per e-fold of steps. The existing loader_frac telemetry is NOT sufficient for this: it measures CPU time inside next(train_loader), which overlaps GPU execution by construction and therefore cannot tell idleness from overlap.
competing_explanation: HOST CPU CONTENTION, which sets the packing time and is the dominant nuisance on this shared 192-core box: byte-identical control code has ranged 621 to 1021 steps, and L006 shows even the taskset core block moves the packing loop by 2.43 ms/step. Slack is therefore a property of the run's host load, not a constant of the system -- and it moves the FLATTERING way, since heavier host load slows packing and makes GPU work look freer. A treatment that appears free may simply have landed in a high-contention wave. Discriminating observations: read gpu_slack_frac off the yoked control of the SAME wave rather than from any earlier run; require the counterbalanced slot swap of L013 on the same 96-107/108-119 core pair; and report the treatment's added FLOPs as a fraction of the CONTROL's gpu_span_ms_med, so the headroom claim is stated against a concurrently measured denominator.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-WRONG (kills the mechanism): an arm that raises gpu_span_ms_med by 20% or more also raises step_ms_med by a comparable fraction, in a run whose measured gpu_slack_frac was above 0.3. That would mean the slack is not spendable -- most likely because the binding CPU cost is kernel-LAUNCH time in the main thread rather than GPU execution, in which case adding operations costs launches and the whole 'GPU capacity is free' framing of this campaign is wrong. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: gpu_span_ms_med does not move when FLOPs are added, meaning the FLOPs were never added or the events are timing an already-drained queue -- re-run, score nothing. NOTE the asymmetry that makes this mechanism useful: a FLOP-adding arm whose gpu_span_ms_med rises while step_ms_med and num_steps stay inside the yoked control's band CONFIRMS it, whatever val_bpb does. val_bpb is not this mechanism's endpoint; wall-clock price is.
mediator: The per-step overlap slack between the asynchronous GPU queue and the synchronous single-threaded CPU packing loop: slack_ms = step_ms - gpu_span_ms. The training loop calls next(train_loader) AFTER loss.backward() inside the gradient-accumulation loop (baseline/train.py:553-559) with no synchronization until train_loss.item(), so the CPU packs micro-batch k+1 while the GPU executes micro-batch k, and the step costs max(CPU, GPU) rather than their sum. With loader_frac measured around 0.94 of charged time, the GPU is the shorter leg by an order of magnitude, and the mediator is how much GPU work can be added before it stops being. This mechanism prices FLOPs; it does not promise loss. Its two directional consequences are what make it worth a record: added GPU work is free in wall-clock until the slack is consumed, and removed GPU work buys nothing -- which is exactly what L011 measured when 40% fewer Newton-Schulz iterations returned 0.2% of step time.
name: loader_slack_prices_gpu_flops_at_zero
notes: NOT implemented -- new instrumentation only, no math change, and it belongs in the shared telemetry block of tools/make_variant.py so the control emits it too. It touches nothing inside muon_step_fused. This mechanism is the price sheet the other five need: periln_branch_output_norm, qk_norm_pins_attention_logit_scale and mtp_supervision_density all change GPU work, and none of their val_bpb deltas can be separated from the step law without it. Note also that tools/direction.py registers 'prefetch' as the input_pipeline mechanism, which attacks the SAME quantity from the other side (reclaiming the GPU-serialized remainder) and is bounded by it: with gpu_slack_frac near 0.9 the entire prize for perfect overlap is the ~10% GPU share, whereas the slack available to SPEND is nine times larger. prefetch is also, as of this record, not implemented in tools/make_variant.py at all.

activation_observable: input_embed_learned_params_M -- learned parameters in the token -> d_model map, in millions. Control reads 16.777216 (32768 x 512); the treatment must read the size of the projection alone (D x 512, i.e. well under 1.0). Emitted by every arm. Paired with kron_code_collision_frac, the fraction of vocabulary entries whose fixed code is bit-identical to another entry's, which must be 0.000000 -- this is the degenerate-engagement guard, and without it a collapsed codec would present as a clean null. num_params_M (already printed) must be reported with them, because the intervention removes ~13% of the model's parameters and no comparison is interpretable without that on the record.
competing_explanation: A CAPACITY AND OPTIMIZER-GROUP CHANGE, not a representation-sharing effect. Deleting 16.78M AdamW-owned parameters at embedding_lr 0.2 simultaneously (a) shrinks the model by ~13%, (b) removes the second-highest-gradient-variance tensor in the model from the optimizer entirely, and (c) at final_epoch 2.0, where the data is seen twice, removes the parameters most able to memorize token identity. Any of the three is a cheaper explanation of a win than byte-structure sharing. Discriminating observations: an arm that KEEPS the free table but cuts embedding_lr (if the win is a step-size effect it reproduces there), and an arm using a RANDOM fixed code of the same D with the same projection instead of the byte code -- if random codes win equally, the effect is 'freeze and project the input map', and the byte structure the source paper credits is doing nothing. That random-code arm is the single most informative follow-up and costs the same slot.
falsifier: ENGAGED-AND-INERT: input_embed_learned_params_M drops from ~16.78 to under 1.0 and kron_code_collision_frac is 0, yet val_bpb is inside 0.000174 of the yoked control -- the 0.083 +/- 0.007 nat win reported at GPT-2 124M does not transfer to a 32768-token vocabulary in a model that already RMS-normalizes the embedding output (baseline/train.py:281) and already carries separate per-layer value embeddings on half its layers, which give the token identity a second, independent learned path into the network that the source model did not have. ENGAGED-AND-DEGENERATE, which must not be scored as inert: kron_code_collision_frac > 0 means distinct tokens share an identical code and are indistinguishable at the input, so the model is provably handicapped and the arm measures the codec's construction, not the mechanism. DID-NOT-ENGAGE: input_embed_learned_params_M still reads ~16.78 -- the free table is still there.
mediator: The number of independently learned parameters per token identity in the input map, and therefore how many gradient updates each input code receives. The baseline learns a free 512-dim row for each of 32768 tokens (16.78M parameters, bf16, AdamW at embedding_lr 0.2): a rare token's row is updated only on the steps where that token appears, so its representation is a function of its own frequency. Replacing the table with a FIXED byte-structure code C[v] in R^D (built once at startup from the frozen tokenizer's per-token byte string) followed by a single learned D x 512 projection makes every token's input vector a function of one matrix that EVERY token in EVERY batch updates. Frequency-dependent under-training of the input map is replaced by parameter sharing across tokens that share bytes.
name: kronecker_byte_input_code
notes: NOT implemented -- new generator code, entirely inside train.py. SCOPE, stated plainly: prepare.py is frozen and this mechanism does not modify it. It changes no loader, no tokenization and no data order; it reads the frozen tokenizer's vocabulary once at startup (tokenizer.decode per token id, 32768 calls) to build a constant matrix, and startup is not charged against the 300-second budget, which is accumulated per-step from step 11 onward. If the operator reads the freeze as 'no tokenizer involvement of any kind', this mechanism is out of scope and the input_pipeline family has ZERO reachable mechanisms, because its only other usable claim (b2_seqlen_extension_worse_than_microbatch_for_batch_growth) is about reaching a larger batch by extending sequence length, and MAX_SEQ_LEN is defined in the frozen prepare.py. b1_kronecker_byte_embed_124m_win is the highest-transfer claim in the entire registry (transfer 4, 3 seeds per arm, 18/18 cells favouring the treatment, measured at exactly 124M) and it is filed under a family that has no other reachable lever; that mismatch is the finding, and it should be resolved by an explicit scope ruling rather than by leaving the claim unused.

activation_observable: flops_per_token_M: 289.4 means engaged (control 239.1, mlp=3 arm 213.9). It is computed by estimate_flops() by walking the CONSTRUCTED modules, not by echoing the cfg, so it proves the model really changed -- the same reason the depth print was moved from the DEPTH constant to config.n_layer. Because the mediator is the exchange rate rather than the FLOPs themselves, add gpu_wait_frac (NEW): accumulate perf_counter around `train_loss_f = train_loss.item()` and around the terminal `torch.cuda.synchronize()` for steps > 10 into the `_t_wait` accumulator that the shared instrumentation block already declares and never fills, then print `gpu_wait_frac: {_t_wait/total_training_time:.6f}` beside loader_frac. Emit it in the CONTROL too, so it is a comparison and not a bare number; it is a supporting diagnostic and the verdict still rests on the controlled step-count comparison, per the standing rule that no claim about where the 300 seconds goes may come from reading timing fields alone. All of it runs in the epilogue after the charged clock has stopped, and nothing is added inside muon_step_fused.
competing_explanation: 'It just changed step count.' Adding FLOPs can only remove steps here, so the cheap explanation for any val_bpb movement is the step law alone: predicted delta = -0.063 * ln(num_steps_treatment / num_steps_control), computed against the YOKED control of the same wave (L005 -- host load, not our code, sets step count, and byte-identical code has ranged 621 to 1021 steps). The discriminating observation is the pair (step_ms_med, num_steps) read together with flops_per_token_M: if measured delta agrees with the step-law prediction to within the counterbalanced resolution, nothing was learned about capacity and only the exchange rate was measured; the mechanism survives only if val_bpb beats its own step-law prediction. Second competing explanation, specific to changing capacity: WEIGHT_DECAY is a fixed 0.2 with no width scaling, and b1_indep_wd_scales_inverse_width reports that failing to scale independent WD with width costs as much as dropping muP entirely -- so a null could be a mis-tuned decay rather than a saturated capacity. mlp ratio is the right first arm precisely because it leaves model_dim at 512, so the AdamW 1/sqrt(dim) rescale and the Muon max(1, m/n)^0.5 shape factor for the 512x512 blocks are untouched; only c_fc/c_proj change shape (2048->3072 rows), whose Muon shape factor moves from 2.0 to 2.449. Report peak_vram_mb as well: 45060 MB of ~143 GB at baseline, so VRAM cannot be the confound, and if it moves unexpectedly the build did something other than what was asked.
falsifier: Run mlp=6 (+21.1% FLOPs) and mlp=3 (-10.5% FLOPs) as slot-counterbalanced pairs against the byte-identical control and regress step_ms_med on flops_per_token_M. DID NOT ENGAGE: flops_per_token_M is still 239.1 (the mlp substitution did not apply -- make_variant only edits the two nn.Linear lines when mlp != 4, so a mis-typed cfg leaves a byte-different file with an identical model, the L007 failure shape). ENGAGED AND THERE IS NO SLACK: flops_per_token_M = 289.4 and step_ms_med rises by >=18% (i.e. slope >= 0.85 of proportional), which says the GPU is already the critical path, kills this mechanism outright, and retires the whole 'GPU capacity is nearly free' premise for every other capacity proposal -- that alone is worth the two slots. ENGAGED, SLACK EXISTS, CAPACITY IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: step_ms_med rises <5%, gpu_wait_frac falls toward 0 in the treatment, and val_bpb is inside the counterbalanced resolution of 0.000174 -- the FLOPs were free and the model did not want them. A LOSS with step_ms_med flat is also informative and is not a 'did not engage': it says added MLP capacity is actively harmful at 1000 steps and closes the direction upward.
mediator: GPU-busy time per step that is NOT on the wall-clock critical path, i.e. the marginal exchange rate d(step_ms)/d(flops_per_token). This is DEFINED to be measured by a controlled FLOP change, not inferred from the timing fields: fwdbwd_frac 0.059 is CPU kernel-LAUNCH time and says nothing about GPU occupancy, and a previous campaign built a whole strategy on misreading it. What can be stated without a run is only an arithmetic bound -- 239.1 MFLOP/token x 524288 tokens / 0.2976 s = 421 TFLOP/s sustained, 42.6% of the 989.5 TF bf16 peak the script assumes -- which bounds but does not determine occupancy, because these are 512-wide GEMMs whose achievable rate is itself unknown here. The physical quantity this mechanism changes is how much arithmetic is added per step -- MLP hidden width (mlp 4 -> 6) raises flops_per_token from 239.1 M to 289.4 M (+21.1%) and non-embedding parameters from 29.4 M to 37.7 M (+28.6%) while leaving the CPU packing loop, the token budget and the data order bit-identical. It is NOT the knob 'mlp': the same +21% could be bought with dim or depth, and what is being measured is the exchange rate d(step_ms)/d(flops_per_token), which is the number that decides whether ANY claim in the capacity family is actionable at a fixed 300 s. The campaign's written cost model is not usable here: it was calibrated in the 621-815 step / final_epoch 1.0 regime (L005_operating_point_moved_v2) and the L011 datum that 40% of the Newton-Schulz iterations is worth 0.2% of step time is a statement about a few hundred MFLOP of tiny 512x512 Gram matrices, not about a 50 GFLOP/step change in the MLP GEMMs. Direction and magnitude, stated in advance: this INCREASES FLOPs and can only lose steps, never gain them; at the pessimistic end (GPU fully on the critical path) step_ms rises 21%, num_steps falls from ~1019 to ~841, and the campaign step law (-0.063 bpb per e-fold of steps) charges +0.0148 bpb that the added capacity must beat; at the optimistic end (fully hidden) the capacity is free. Worth it because the run is over-tokened, not under-tokened: 1019 x 524288 = 534 M tokens against 29.4 M FLOP-active parameters is 18.2 tokens/param (10.6 on all 50.3 M), where b1_muon_optimal_tpp_lower puts Muon's compute-optimal ratio at 7.4 -- every registered allocation claim says this operating point should spend on parameters and not on tokens.
name: flop_slack_exchange_rate

activation_observable: n_embd: 640.0 means engaged (control prints 512.0), read together with depth: 5.0 (control 8.0) and n_ve_layers: 3.0 (control 4.0). All three are already emitted by every variant, computed from the constructed model. The iso-budget precondition is flops_per_token_M: 234.0 (control 239.1, i.e. -2.1%) -- if that number is not in [231.7, 236.3] the arm is not iso-FLOP and the comparison is void before val_bpb is read.
competing_explanation: 'It just changed step count.' Even at matched FLOPs the two shapes need not run at the same speed: 640-wide GEMMs with 5 heads may hit a different cuDNN/FA3 tile than 512-wide with 4, and depth 5 issues 37.5% fewer kernels per step. The discriminating observation is num_steps against the yoked control: if it differs by more than 2% the verdict must be reported as step-law-corrected (-0.063 bpb per e-fold) and flagged, not pooled. Three further cheaper explanations must be named because depth cannot be moved in isolation in this file: (1) WINDOW_PATTERN 'SSSL' with the forced-long last layer gives 2 long of 8 layers at depth 8 but 2 long of 5 at depth 5, so the long-attention fraction rises 25% -> 40% and part of any win is an attention-budget change, testable by re-running the winner with win='SSSSL'; (2) has_ve alternating gives 4/8 VE layers at depth 8 and 3/5 at depth 5, so value-embedding density rises 50% -> 60% and overlaps value_embedding_density, testable by the ve axis; (3) the AdamW learning rates are auto-scaled by (n_embd/768)^-0.5, so moving 512 -> 640 silently drops the embedding, unembedding and scalar LRs by 10.6% while the Muon matrix LR is unchanged -- a null could be a detuned embedding LR rather than a flat aspect-ratio response.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: the run prints n_embd 512 or depth 8 -- these are printed from config.n_embd / config.n_layer (the model), not from the DEPTH constant, precisely because the constant lied once before; or flops_per_token_M is outside 234.0 +/- 1%, meaning the arm is not the iso-FLOP arm that was designed and any val_bpb difference is a capacity change wearing an aspect-ratio label. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: n_embd 640, depth 5, flops_per_token_M 234.0, num_steps within 2% of the yoked control, and |delta val_bpb| < 0.000174 -- at 50 M parameters and 1000 steps the aspect ratio in the range 64-128 dim-per-layer is flat, and the capacity family should stop spending slots on shape and spend them on total size instead. The claim that motivates this is measured at 3 B parameters and 250 B tokens (128 vs 512 layers), a 60x scale gap, and its own authors report the DOWNSTREAM average did not follow the training-loss ordering (52.2 vs 52.3) -- so a null here is a genuine transfer failure and must be recorded as one, not as a broken run. The mirror arm depth 14 / n_embd 384 is the deep direction, but it is only matched to +5.5% params / +5.6% FLOPs and its verdict must therefore be step-law-corrected; run it only if the wide arm moves.
mediator: How a FIXED parameter and FLOP budget is divided between residual width (the rank of the stream every layer reads and writes, and the width of every GEMM) and the number of sequential nonlinear transformations applied to it. depth 8 / n_embd 512 -> depth 5 / n_embd 640 moves from 8 sequential blocks of 4 heads to 5 blocks of 5 heads while holding total parameters at 50.79 M vs 50.33 M (+0.9%) and flops_per_token at 234.0 M vs 239.1 M (-2.1%) -- the closest iso-capacity, iso-FLOP aspect-ratio pair reachable given that n_embd must be a multiple of HEAD_DIM=128. The mediator is not 'depth' and not 'dim'; either alone changes the budget. Because the FLOPs are matched to 2%, this mechanism is nearly free of the exchange-rate uncertainty that flop_slack_exchange_rate exists to measure, which is why it is worth running even before that exchange rate is known. It also raises per-GEMM arithmetic intensity (640-wide instead of 512-wide) while cutting the number of kernel launches per step by 37.5%, both of which help a step whose CPU launch time is only 6% but whose GPU efficiency at 512 width is unmeasured.
name: iso_capacity_aspect_ratio

activation_observable: tokens_per_step: 262144.0 means engaged (control prints 524288.0), with grad_accum: 1.0 (control 2.0). Both are already printed by every variant. The number that makes the result INTERPRETABLE rather than merely engaged is total_tokens_M (already printed): the mechanism's claim is 'more updates at essentially the same tokens', so total_tokens_M in the treatment must stay within 10% of the yoked control's, and the verdict text must quote it. Add tokens_per_sec_med (NEW, one line in the epilogue: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE/median(_dts), the _dts list already exists) so that the invariance of the packing-loop throughput -- the entire premise of the mechanism -- is measured rather than assumed: engaged and premise-confirmed means tokens_per_sec_med within 10% of the control's ~1.76 M tokens/s.
competing_explanation: 'It just changed step count', and here that is not a nuisance to be excluded but the hypothesis itself, so the usual step-law correction must NOT be applied. The campaign's -0.063 bpb per e-fold of steps was fitted where step count moved because host CPU contention moved (L005, L006), i.e. where steps and TOKENS moved together; applying it to an arm that changes steps at approximately constant tokens double-counts and would convert a genuine token-limited null into a fake 'underperforms the step law' verdict. The discriminating observation is total_tokens_M together with tokens_per_sec_med: same tokens + more updates + better loss = the batch was above critical (mechanism confirmed); same tokens + more updates + no change = update-saturated; fewer tokens + more updates + better loss = tokens were not the constraint either, and the direction to push is smaller batches still (tbs 2**17 needs dbs 64). Second competing explanation: the learning rate was not retuned. b3_lmo_optlr_rises_with_batch_falls_with_tokens says the optimal LR RISES with batch size, so halving the batch at fixed MATRIX_LR=0.04 leaves the LR too high -- the bias runs AGAINST the treatment, so a win is strong evidence and a loss is ambiguous between 'batch too small' and 'LR now mistuned'. This asymmetry must be stated in the verdict, and a loss should be followed by an LR-corrected arm before the direction is closed.
falsifier: The two rival hypotheses make quantitatively separated predictions, which is the point of the design. UPDATE-LIMITED: val_bpb improves by roughly -0.063*ln(1.84) + 0.063*ln(1.09) = -0.033 bpb. TOKEN-LIMITED: val_bpb is flat or slightly worse (+0.005), because the run sees 8% fewer tokens and updates are already past saturation. The gap between the two predictions is 0.038 bpb, 220x the counterbalanced resolution of 0.000174, so one slot-swapped pair settles it. DID NOT ENGAGE: tokens_per_step still prints 524288 (the TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE substitution is unconditional in make_variant, so this would mean the queue shipped the wrong variant -- L009), or grad_accum is not 1. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: tokens_per_step 262144, grad_accum 1, num_steps up >=60%, total_tokens_M within 10% of the yoked control, and |delta val_bpb| < 0.000174 -- the batch was at or below critical already and the whole token_exposure axis is closed downward, which is a real result. THIRD, DISQUALIFYING OUTCOME: total_tokens_M falls by more than 20%, meaning per-step overhead is larger than assumed and the arm traded tokens for updates rather than converting one into the other; the comparison is then confounded and must be re-run at tbs 2**18 with dbs 256... i.e. it cannot be fixed by dbs, so it must be reported as inconclusive rather than as a null.
mediator: The number of optimizer updates the run performs per token consumed -- equivalently, the ratio of the global batch to the critical batch size at this loss level. TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**18 halves tokens_per_step from 524288 to 262144 and, uniquely on this benchmark, does so at almost no cost in tokens: the throughput bottleneck is the frozen best-fit packing loop in prepare.py, whose cost is per ROW built (row_capacity = T+1, an O(len(doc_buffer)=1000) scan per document placement) and therefore per TOKEN, not per step, and it owns loader_frac 0.66-0.68 of the charged 297 ms. Halving tokens per step halves the rows built per step, so tokens/second is invariant to first order and the intervention converts token throughput into update throughput at a near-1:1 rate. Expected: step_ms_med ~297 -> ~160-190, num_steps ~1019 -> ~1580-1875, total_tokens_M 534 -> 415-490 (-8% to -22%, from per-step overheads that do not shrink: optimizer.step over 32 stacked matrices, the .item() sync, the terminal synchronize). The mediator is NOT 'token exposure' and NOT step count as a proxy for tokens -- those two are deliberately decoupled here, which is exactly what makes this the sharpest experiment available in this family. 524288 tokens per update for a 50 M-parameter model is a very large batch; b2_optimal_batch_size_grows_as_training_progresses says the optimal batch is SMALLEST at the start of training and this entire run is the start.
name: batch_above_critical_at_fixed_tokens

activation_observable: ramped_step_frac (NEW): count steps executed while `_ramped` is True and print `ramped_step_frac: {n_ramped/step:.6f}` in the epilogue. ENGAGED = strictly between 0 and 1, expected ~0.33 because post-ramp steps consume twice the tokens and take roughly twice as long, so half the TIME is a third of the STEPS. 0.0 or 1.0 means not engaged. Report alongside the already-printed grad_accum (2.0 at end = the ramp fired and stuck) and tokens_per_step (524288, the post-ramp value, which is why grad_accum rather than tokens_per_step is the discriminator against the control).
competing_explanation: 'It just changed step count' -- the ramp lowers total steps relative to the flat tbs=18 arm and raises them relative to the control, so a naive step-law reading explains any ordering. The discriminating observation is the pair (total_tokens_M, ramped_step_frac): the mechanism's claim is that at MATCHED total tokens the ramp beats both flat batches, so the verdict must quote total_tokens_M for all three arms and be void if they spread by more than 10%. Second and more dangerous competing explanation: the ramp is confounded with a learning-rate event. make_variant multiplies every param group's LR by sqrt(2) at the switch, so 'ramp helps' could be 'a mid-run LR bump helps' -- and b3_optimal_lr_scales_iters_minus_one_third independently says the optimal LR depends on the iteration count, which the ramp also changes. The clean discriminator is an LR-only arm: the same sqrt(2) multiplier applied at progress 0.5 with grad_accum held at its base value. Do not report a positive ramp verdict without it.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: ramped_step_frac prints 0.0 (the ramp predicate never became true) or 1.0 (it was true from step 0), or grad_accum prints 1 at the end instead of 2. Either means the arm ran as a flat-batch run and its val_bpb is a duplicate of another arm rather than a test of the schedule -- exactly the failure mode L007 describes, where a variant differs in source but not in behaviour and still gets counted against an axis. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: ramped_step_frac in [0.25, 0.45], grad_accum 2, and val_bpb indistinguishable from the flat tbs=18 arm within 0.000174, which says the second half's batch size is irrelevant and only the early phase carries the effect -- a positive finding that redirects the family toward the first 50% of the run. THE VERDICT IS THREE-WAY, not two-way: ramp vs control, ramp vs flat-small, flat-small vs control, and all three must be counterbalanced pairs on the SAME core-block pair (L013) or the comparison is not a comparison. Kill condition for the mechanism: ramp is WORSE than flat-small AND worse than control, which would mean the sqrt(2) LR bump at the switch is a schedule shock rather than a batch effect.
mediator: The TIME PROFILE of updates-per-token across the run, rather than its average. Gradient noise relative to the signal is largest at the start, so the batch that minimizes tokens-to-target-loss is smallest early and grows monotonically as the loss falls; a single fixed batch is therefore wrong at one end of the run whichever value is chosen. This arm starts at 262144 tokens/update and doubles to the baseline 524288 at 50% of the charged clock (cfg tbs=18 with batch_ramp=0.5, which doubles grad_accum and multiplies every group's LR by sqrt(2) after the switch), so it ENDS at exactly the control's operating point and differs only in the first half. Distinguishing it from batch_above_critical_at_fixed_tokens is the whole point: that mechanism says the batch is too large everywhere, this one says it is too large only early. They are jointly identified by running both against one control -- ramp better than flat-small says the crossover of b2_batchsize_loss_curves_cross_under_constant_lr is inside our 300 s, flat-small better than ramp says it is not reached at all.
name: rising_critical_batch_schedule

activation_observable: n_ve_layers: 8.0 means the density changed (control prints 4.0; ve=4 arm prints 2.0) -- already emitted by every variant, counted off the constructed module dict rather than the cfg. The number that separates 'present' from 'used' is ve_gate_w_absmin (NEW, epilogue, zero cost, no graph break): min over VE-carrying layers of mean(|block.attn.ve_gate.weight|). Every ve_gate is initialised to EXACTLY zero, so this is 0.0 at step 0 by construction and any value above ~1e-4 proves that the least-used of the eight tables learned an input-dependent gate. Emit it in the control too (it is well defined there over 4 layers), so 'engaged' is a comparison. Optionally also ve_emb_rms, the rms of the value_embeds weights, whose init value is n_embd^-0.5 = 0.0442 -- drift off 0.0442 proves the tables themselves trained and not just the gates.
competing_explanation: 'It just changed step count.' Here that is unusually easy to exclude because flops_per_token_M is IDENTICAL between arms by construction (239.1 in both), so any step-count movement must come from the extra embedding gathers, the sparse gradient scatter and 4 extra AdamW states, not from arithmetic. The discriminating observation is num_steps together with peak_vram_mb: if num_steps is within 1% of the yoked control the val_bpb delta is attributable to the mechanism with no step-law correction at all, which makes this the cleanest arm in the whole set; if num_steps drops more than 1%, the embedding traffic is on the critical path and the verdict must be step-law-corrected. peak_vram_mb should rise from 45060 MB by roughly 100-150 MB (bf16 weights plus bf16 AdamW moments), on a device with ~143 GB, so VRAM is not a confound and an unexpected jump means the build did something else. Second competing explanation, and the reason the Kronecker claims are cited on BOTH sides: b1_kronecker_untied_confound reports that a headline embedding-path win was partly just +3.1 M extra parameters in an untied head. Our arm is +16.78 M parameters, so a win here is likewise ambiguous between 'value embeddings specifically' and 'more parameters anywhere'. The discriminating follow-up is a FLOP-matched parameter control that spends a comparable number of parameters somewhere else -- mlp 4 -> 6 is +8.4 M and is already the flop_slack_exchange_rate arm, so the two mechanisms cross-check each other and should be queued in the same block.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: n_ve_layers prints 4.0 (the has_ve substitution did not apply), or ve_gate_w_absmin is ~0.0 (< 1e-5) while n_ve_layers is 8, which means the newly added tables were carried but never used -- their gates are still at their zero init, sigmoid(0)*2 = 1.0 neutral, and the arm is a parameter-count change with no functional change. Those are different failures and must be reported differently: the first is a build bug, the second says the value path cannot absorb more lookup capacity at this horizon, which is itself the answer b0_groupmuon_v_projection_no_gain predicts. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: n_ve_layers 8.0, ve_gate_w_absmin > 1e-4, num_steps within 1% of the yoked control, and |delta val_bpb| < 0.000174 -- free parameters in the value path do not buy loss at 534 M tokens, and the ve axis closes upward. The horizon objection is answerable in advance: b1_kronecker_gap_grows_with_steps measured an embedding-path intervention at 0.071 of its final 0.083 nats by step 1000, so ~85% of an embedding-side effect is available inside our ~1019 steps and a null cannot be dismissed as 'too early'.
mediator: The fraction of layers whose attention VALUE path is fed directly by a token-identity lookup table rather than only by the residual stream. has_ve currently gives 4 of 8 layers a private vocab x 512 embedding that is added to v through a zero-initialised per-head sigmoid gate; the ve axis changes the stride, and ve=1 puts one on every layer. The physical quantity is parameters placed where they cost NO FLOPs: value embeddings are excluded from estimate_flops by construction, so ve 2 -> 1 moves total parameters from 50.33 M to 67.11 M (+33.3%) while flops_per_token_M stays at exactly 239.1 M and every GEMM in the model is unchanged. The only added work is 4 more gather/scatter pairs over an 8192 x 512 bf16 table and 4 more AdamW states -- roughly 1 GB/step of extra HBM traffic against 4.8 TB/s, well under 1 ms. This is the single largest capacity lever in the system that does not touch the FLOP budget, and it is only visible once the real configuration is read rather than assumed: VOCAB_SIZE is 8192, not 32768, so the model is 50.3 M parameters and not the 124 M the campaign's operating-point description states, and value embeddings are already 16.78 M of it -- 33% of all parameters, four times the size of wte plus lm_head combined. The reverse arm ve=4 (2 VE layers, 41.94 M params, -16.7%) tests the same mediator downward and costs nothing extra to queue.
name: value_embedding_density

activation_observable: qk_block_sv_ratio (NEW): every 100 steps, snapshot one probe layer's c_q weight before and after optimizer.step(), take the delta, and report the mean over its four 128x512 head blocks of singular_value_min / singular_value_max (torch.linalg.svdvals on a 128x512 matrix, microseconds, done in MuonAdamW._step_muon OUTSIDE the @torch.compile(fullgraph=True) muon_step_fused, which is left byte-identical apart from the reshape). Print the run mean as qk_block_sv_ratio. ENGAGED = >= 0.9 in the treatment: each head block is separately driven to flat singular values by the iteration. The CONTROL emits the same number and will sit clearly below it, because a 128-row slice of a 512x512 orthogonalized update is not itself well conditioned -- so this is a self-contained engagement test with a comparison built in, in the style of secmom_ortho_ratio rather than a flag that says the edit should have applied.
competing_explanation: 'It just changed step count.' The reshaped iteration is genuinely cheaper -- 4 x 128^2 x 512 versus 512^3 MACs per matrix per iteration -- so a win could be bought steps rather than a better update direction. L011 measured that removing 40% of the Newton-Schulz iterations moved step_ms_med by only ~0.2% (299.45 vs 300.01, and the treatment gained no steps), so the predicted step gain here is below the noise; the discriminating observation is that num_steps must be within 0.5% and step_ms_med within 1 ms of the yoked control, and if either moves more, the verdict is step-law-corrected and reported as contaminated. Second competing explanation: splitting c_q and c_k out of the shared 512x512 shape group changes which tensors get stacked together, and stacking order affects nothing mathematically but does change kernel shapes and the NorMuon buffer layout -- so an IDENTITY arm is required, in which c_q/c_k are moved to their own Muon group with NO reshape. If that arm alone moves val_bpb beyond resolution, the grouping and not the orthogonalization granularity is the cause, and this mechanism is refuted whatever the treatment does.
falsifier: DID NOT ENGAGE: qk_block_sv_ratio in the treatment is indistinguishable from the control's, meaning the reshape never reached the iteration -- the likely build failures are that c_q/c_k were not split out of the shared 512x512 shape group, or that the second_momentum_buffer was allocated at (N, 512, 1) while the update was reshaped, in which case the run would more likely crash than silently no-op. ENGAGED AND DID NOTHING: qk_block_sv_ratio >= 0.9 in the treatment against a control value well below it, num_steps within 0.5% of the yoked control, and |delta val_bpb| < 0.000174 -- the per-head split does not transfer to 8 layers / 4 heads / 1019 steps, and the attention_detail family should be closed until a claim measured at THIS depth appears. A LOSS is also a real result and is what the V-projection claim predicts by analogy, and it would additionally serve as a second positive control for the harness (the only one so far is ns=3, L010). Run the negative control if and only if the Q/K arm moves: the same grouping applied to c_v alone must NOT reproduce the effect; if it does, the mediator is 'per-128-row-block orthogonalization of any projection' and not anything about queries and keys.
mediator: The GRANULARITY at which the polar/Newton-Schulz iteration enforces orthogonality on the query and key projection updates. Muon currently stacks every 512x512 matrix in a shape group and orthogonalizes each as one 512x512 object, so the update mixes all heads' output subspaces; grouping by head instead reshapes the stacked update from (N, 512, 512) to (N*4, 128, 512) before the iteration and back after it, so each head's 128 output rows are made mutually orthogonal WITHIN the head while nothing is enforced ACROSS heads. Total update magnitude is preserved exactly and needs no LR transfer: a 512x512 orthogonal matrix and four stacked semi-orthogonal 128x512 blocks both have Frobenius norm sqrt(512), and forcing red_dim=-1 keeps the NorMuon reduction axis (per output row) bit-identical to the baseline, so the ONLY thing that changes is the direction of the update. The iteration also gets cheaper (four 128x128 Gram matrices instead of one 512x512), which by L011's measurement is worth ~0 wall clock and is therefore not a confound. This is the mechanism the attention_detail claims actually support, and their operating point is the closest match in the entire registry: GPT-2 Small, Muon on a modded-nanogpt recipe, 524288 tokens per optimizer step -- identical to ours -- with the finest split winning EARLY and being overtaken by g=6 only in the middle/late stage of a 6200-step run. Our run is 1019 steps, entirely inside the region where the claims say fine splitting leads. Applied to Q and K only: b0_groupmuon_v_projection_no_gain is the registered negative control saying the same treatment on V buys nothing.
name: qk_head_grouped_orthogonalization

activation_observable: secmom_ortho_ratio, which must fall far below 1 to show the buffer left orthogonalized scale, AND secmom_clamp_frac, which must stay near 0 to show it did not fall off the bottom instead. Either alone is insufficient: the ratio rule passed on all three non-engaged runs.
competing_explanation: an effective learning-rate change. Renormalizing the momentum before orthogonalization alters the norm of the matrix fed to the polar iteration, and the iteration's output scale is set by that input; so a win could be nothing but a global step-size change that the same wave would reproduce by moving lr alone. This must be ruled out with an LR-matched arm or by showing the post-NS RMS is preserved. NEW OPPOSING EVIDENCE, registered after the run: a transfer-4 claim from a paper measured at 124M-class scale and exactly 524288 tokens/step reports row-wise second-moment normalization working BETTER after Newton-Schulz than before, which is the baseline's ordering. This mechanism is now a contested bet rather than a favoured one, and a null from the corrected implementation should be read as corroborating that claim.
falsifier: val_bpb of the reordered variant is within the measured within-wave band of its yoked control WHILE the activation observable shows the preconditioner is materially non-identity (pre-NS entrywise rescale ratio far from 1). That combination says the intervention engaged and did nothing. If instead the observable shows the rescale ratio sitting at ~1, the run is INCONCLUSIVE about the mechanism, not evidence against it.
measured_outcome: NOT REFUTED -- NOT ENGAGED. Three runs (precond_pre_slot0, precond_pre_slot1, precond_pre_R1P_C) reported secmom_clamp_frac 0.99789, 0.99791 and 0.99791 against 0.00000 in every yoked control, so 99.8% of the second-moment buffer sat at the clamp_min(1e-10) floor and the arm ran as plain Muon minus NorMuon. The val_bpb deltas (+0.001288, -0.000433, +0.000809) are therefore INCONCLUSIVE about this mechanism. See L014_precond_clamped_out_did_not_engage.
mediator: the entrywise scale distribution of the momentum matrix AT THE MOMENT it enters Newton-Schulz. Orthogonalization is scale-equivariant in a way that discards entrywise second-moment information: normalizing the momentum by its running second moment BEFORE the polar iteration changes which singular directions the iteration is asked to equalize, whereas the same normalization applied AFTER only rescales an already-orthogonalized update and cannot change its direction. IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTED: the momentum is now rescaled to unit RMS per matrix before the second moment is taken, which puts the buffer back in the range its floor and zero-init were designed for. The rescale is a per-matrix scalar and the polar iteration opens by dividing by the Frobenius norm, so it cannot smuggle in an effective learning-rate change.
name: precond_before_ortho_v2_rms_normalized

activation_observable: mean Frobenius norm of the Muon-owned stacked matrices at the final step, printed as muon_weight_norm_final, together with the fraction of entries the cautious mask actually decayed, printed as wd_mask_frac -- the second number is what distinguishes a nominal coefficient change from a delivered one.

A registered claim puts the equilibrium timescale at order 1000 steps for typical eta/lambda, so at ~1000 steps any effect may be an implicit warmup-shape change rather than the steady-state regularization the source papers measured, and the two are not distinguishable from the final loss alone.

Note one registered claim holds that Muon without weight decay converges FASTER initially, so this mechanism predicts a sign that may invert at our very short horizon; a null here is genuinely informative. The upward direction has now fired. The remaining live question is DOWNWARD -- wd_const=0.0 -- which one registered claim predicts helps at short horizons and another predicts hurts; that disagreement is unresolved and is the experiment worth a slot.

The baseline applies a CAUTIOUS decay, masked to entries where update and parameter agree in sign, so the decay actually delivered to those matrices is strictly less than the nominal coefficient and its effective strength is data-dependent rather than set by the schedule.
name: decay_reaches_muon_matrices_v2_measured
